#6046. United Airlines’ Most Frequent Boeing 777-200 Flights In 2026

The Boeing 777-200 entered service in 1994 and was primarily aimed at US domestic airlines; the 777-200ER followed in 1997 with more of an international focus. The 777-200ER extends the range from around 5,240 nautical miles to 7,065 nautical miles (depending on mission profile). These are workhorses for United's transatlantic routes, as well as some inter-hub routes, routes to Hawaii, and select destinations in East Asia. The type is aging, with older examples struggling with fuel efficiency compared with modern aircraft, although as paid-off aircraft, they also offer much lower capital expenses for United.

Here is what to know about where United Airlines is flying its Boeing 777-200/ER fleet in 2026, according to data provided by Cirium, a data analytics company. The flight data below is for the full 2026 calendar year and includes both the 777-200 and the 777-200ER, as Cirium lacks distinct aircraft codes for the sub-variants. The data is also for the full year, even if the 777s were replaced with other aircraft partway through the year on the routes.

United Airlines operates a fleet of 74 Boeing 777-200/ER airliners, of which Planespotters.net lists 61 as active and 13 as parked. The overall age of the fleet is rapidly aging and is now 27.5 years old. These include 19 Boeing 777-200s, with the remainder being 777-200ERs. United is the launch customer and the largest operator of the 777-200, with the fleet being configured for domestic routes. The 777-200ER includes four examples with domestic configurations. The remainder of the 777-200ER is configured for international operations.

According to Planespotters.net, United has not divested any of its 777-200/ERs since 2005, after eight examples had been transferred to Indian and Brazilian operators. The oldest example in United's service is registered N777UA and was delivered in 1995, making it 31.5 years old. The youngest member of the family is registered as N27015 and was delivered in 2010. It is now around 26.7 years old.

Cirium's data shows United is operating the 777-200/ER from its six main hubs: San Francisco (12,591 route-pair flights), Newark (6,635), Houston (5,549), Washington Dulles (4,900), Denver (3,059), and Chicago O'Hare (1,165). Adding these directly would result in double counting of 1,759 flights due to flights between the hubs. For the full year, United is expected to operate a total of 32,140 flights with the aircraft carrying a total of 9.6 million seats.

Chicago O'Hare sees the fewest flights with United's Boeing 777-200/ERs. Its most frequent pairings (outbound and inbound) are to its other hubs, including 373 flights on the San Francisco pairing (1,604 nautical miles), 309 flights on the Los Angeles pairing (1,517 nautical miles), and 236 flights on the Denver pairing (772 nautical miles). The year is also seeing 174 flights from Chicago to Mexico's Cancun (1,255 nautical miles).

Denver is to see 3,059 United 777-200 family flights carrying 1.1 million seats. Its leading routes by distance and frequency are to Hawaii, including Honolulu (1,226 flights at 2,929 nautical miles), Maui (744 flights at 2,872 nautical miles), and Kona (238 flights at 2,894 nautical miles). That is a total of 2,248 flights on Denver's Hawaii pairings and 73% of the airports' total United 777-200/ER operations.

Other routes include Chicago O'Hare, already mentioned above (236 flights), Houston (225 flights), Cancun (174), as well as a limited number of flights to San Francisco, Orlando, and Washington Dulles. In other words, most of United's non-Hawaii paired 777-200/ER flights from Denver are to its other major hubs in the continental United States.

Examining the busy schedule of one of the most distinguished jets in the world's biggest fleet of airliners.

Washington Dulles has 4,900 United 777-200/ER operations, with the bulk of these being transatlantic flights to Western Europe. Dulles' most frequent pairing is with London Heathrow at 996 flights, followed by Germany's Frankfurt (744 flights). The next most common pairing is transpacific to Tokyo Haneda, with 728 flights. After that Japanese route, it's back to Europe with the pairings to Paris (656 flights), Lisbon (557 flights), and Rome Fiumicino (492 flights).

Other European pairings include Athens (168), Brussels (126), Barcelona (32), and Zurich (18). Domestic routes are to San Francisco (193 flights) and Los Angeles (136 flights). Most European routes from Dulles average between 3,000 and 4,000 nautical miles, although the route to Athens is considerably longer, reaching 4,492 nautical miles. United Airlines dominates Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD), accounting for roughly 66% to 70% of passenger traffic.

From Dulles, United connects the US capital with various intercontinental destinations in Europe, Asia, and even Africa. Somewhat surprisingly, given the US's strong demographic and cultural connections with South America, the only route to that continent operated by United is to São Paulo with Boeing 767-400ERs. Avianca also operates flights between Bogotá and Washington Dulles. The lack of flights is because airlines concentrate US–South America hubs in southern and coastal gateways (Miami, Houston) with stronger passenger demand.

In Houston, George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) is dominated by United Airlines, while William P. Hobby Airport (HOU) is dominated by Southwest Airlines. At IAH, United boasts around 74.1% of the passenger market share, perhaps more now that Spirit has collapsed. Spirit had around 5% of the market share. From Houston, the most frequent 777-200/ER route is to London Heathrow, whose pairing is seeing 1,397 flights in 2026.

Houston is also a significant gateway to South America, with the next busiest pairing being with Buenos Aires (942 flights). The only other South American destination is Chile's Santiago, with 209 flights. These are United's main routes to South America, meaning they aren't used very heavily in that direction. There are no frequent United 777-200/ER routes to Mexico, the Caribbean, or Central America. This is partly due to many of these destinations being within range of narrowbody aircraft. For example, United operates seven daily A320-family flights between Houston and Mexico City.

The third-busiest pairing is with United's West Coast hub of San Francisco (681 flights), with another 225 flights on the Houston-Denver route and 52 flights on the Houston-Newark route. The other regular routes are transatlantic routes to Germany, with the Frankfurt pairing getting 730 flights in 2026 and Munich getting 580. Munich is the longest route at an average distance of 4,708 nautical miles, followed by Frankfurt, Buenos Aires, London Heathrow, and Santiago — all of which are above 4,000 nautical miles.

Two major US airlines currently operate the Boeing 777.

The airport that hosts the second-most United 777-200/ER flights is Newark Liberty, with 6,635 operations. United Airlines holds roughly 60% to 68% of passenger market share at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), making it by far the airport's dominant carrier and largest hub. It is from Newark that United connects the New York region with much of the world, including many transatlantic destinations in Europe.

Even so, the single busiest city pairing is with San Francisco, with 1,314 flights, while the second-busiest transcontinental pairing is with Los Angeles, with 710 flights. Otherwise, transatlantic routes dominate the list and include Paris (863 flights), Dublin (728 flights), Milan (582 flights), London Heathrow (413 flights), Amsterdam (284 flights), Munich (205 flights), Barcelona (184 flights), and Rome (139 flights).

Other notable city pairings include Tokyo Haneda (593 flights) and São Paulo, Brazil (526 flights). The Tokyo route is notable for being one of the longest routes United is assigning its 777-200ERs, at an average distance of 5,877 nautical miles. Currently, United is operating a daily flight to Tokyo Haneda using its 787-9s, suggesting the 777-200ERs have been pulled off the route. United is also operating 787-9s on the twin Newark-Tokyo Narita route.

San Francisco is by far the busiest hub for United's fleet of 777-200/ERs in 2026, with a total of 12,591 operations. Being located on the West Coast, San Francisco also sees the largest range of destinations, with flights to Asia, Australia, New Zealand, Europe, and domestic destinations within the United States. The busiest pairing is the one mentioned above with Newark Liberty (1,314 flights).

European routes include Frankfurt (1,077 flights), London Heathrow (744 flights), Paris (656 flights), Munich (716 flights), Rome (410 flights), Barcelona (266 flights), Zurich (262 flights), and Amsterdam (238 flights). Routes to East Asia are Tokyo Haneda (730), Beijing (728), Osaka (714), Taipei (690), Seoul (273), and Tokyo Narita (239). Already mentioned above are other hub pairings with Houston, Chicago, and Washington.

San Francisco, along with Denver, is a major hub for flights to Hawaii's Honolulu (794). San Francisco is also the only hub where United's 777-200/ERs are flying to Australia (Brisbane with 524 flights and Sydney with 296 flights) and New Zealand (Auckland with 490 flights). The Sydney route is the longest one of all for United's 777-200ERs with an average distance of 6,447 nautical miles followed by Brisbane at 6,140 nautical miles. New Zealand is a bit closer at 5,665 nautical miles.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Booking a table can be the least exciting part of a night out. However, the platform you use to do it can now earn you rewards worth anything from a few cents to a delicious discount on your bill.

OpenTable, DoorDash, Seated and now Resy all reward you for dining out, though each takes a different approach. OpenTable awards its own points, DoorDash issues credits for future orders, Seated offers rewards that can be redeemed for gift cards and Resy awards American Express Membership Rewards points.

As with your favorite coffee chain's loyalty program or a food delivery app subscription, the best option depends on where, how often and how much you eat out. Whichever you choose, you'll generally still earn rewards on eligible restaurant purchases when paying with a dining credit card, making your meal even sweeter.

In this guide, we compare what each program earns, what those rewards are worth and the fine print to watch so you can decide which one deserves a seat at your table.

*Based on TPG's November 2026 valuations.

Related: This overlooked dining program is one of the most generous and gets you $25 off your very first meal

OpenTable Regulars is free to join, and you'll earn 100 dining points for each reservation you book directly on OpenTable while signed in to your account and then complete. Reservations made through restaurant websites or third-party booking partners generally don't qualify. Points are posted only after you've dined, so canceled reservations and no-shows earn nothing.

Some restaurants in the program also offer bonus-point reservations worth 500, 750 or even 1,000 points at certain times. To find them, turn on the "bonus points filter" under special features in the OpenTable app.

Once you have at least 1,000 points, you can redeem them in the app's "Rewards" section at the following rates for U.S. members:

As for the redemption rate you'll get for each, they're:

That means a standard 100-point reservation is only worth 80 cents toward a future meal, and you'll need 20 of them to earn a $16 dining credit, which isn't very rewarding.

Dining credits work at participating OpenTable restaurants (look for the "Dining Credit Accepted" filter). After you redeem your points, you can add the credit to a reservation, which provides a digital Mastercard you can use toward eligible bills. Experience credits work similarly but only apply to certain prepaid experiences, such as prix-fixe menus and cocktail classes. Dining credits expire 12 months after you redeem them.

If you complete six reservations on OpenTable within 12 months, you'll then unlock Gold status for a year. Gold members get priority notifications when tables open up, a three-month complimentary Uber One trial for eligible new or returning members who do not have an active subscription and access to "Gold Tables," which promises harder-to-book tables at more than 500 participating restaurants in over 50 U.S. cities.

OpenTable also partners with Chase, Uber and Visa. Uber One members can book Uber One Exclusive Tables, eligible Visa cardholders can access tables and special events through the Visa Dining Collection and select Chase cardholders get exclusive tables and statement credits (more on that below).

Make sure you're actually turning up for your bookings, though. OpenTable will close your Regulars account and cancel all your points if you record four no-shows within 12 months. Your points also expire after 12 months of inactivity or after 3 years from the date you earn them, whichever comes first.

Related: Earn even more rewards when dining out with OpenTable

DoorDash is best known for delivery, but reservations are now available in select cities across the U.S., Australia and Canada. Its current market page lists 17 U.S. cities, plus Melbourne and Sydney in Australia and Toronto and Vancouver in Canada.

Rather than earn points, you earn promotional DoorDash credits when you book and complete an eligible reservation in the DoorDash app or on its website. The amount is shown before you book and now varies by restaurant, reservation time and membership status. Current U.S. listings commonly advertise $5 in credits, while some times display $10 or $12. Not every reservation earns a credit.

Credits are posted after you've paid for your meal and can be used toward eligible future DoorDash delivery or pickup orders. They typically can't be used to pay for taxes, fees or tips, expire six months after they're issued unless the offer says otherwise, have no cash value and can't be used to buy gift cards or alcohol.

Since the reward is a fixed amount, you don't earn more rewards for a higher food bill. A $5 credit is a 5% return on a $100 dinner but about 1.7% on a $300 tasting menu. A $10 credit would deliver returns of 10% and about 3.3%, respectively. That makes DoorDash Reservations especially appealing for smaller restaurant bills if you already use DoorDash.

DashPass members can earn more on eligible reservations, plus access exclusive prime-time tables and discounts on Lyft Black rides. However, the elevated reservation reward is no longer a simple fixed $2 boost across every listing, so check the offer shown before booking rather than assuming your membership guarantees a particular amount.

Check the restaurant's cancellation policy when you book. Late cancellations and no-shows may incur fees set by the restaurant, and DoorDash says excessive no-shows can result in suspension of your access to reservations.

Outside its reservation cities, DoorDash's "Going Out" tab also lists in-store offers at certain restaurants, with DashPass members earning extra rewards for repeat visits in some locations.

Related: Your complete guide to Chase and DoorDash

What is unique about this program is that you don't need to book through Seated: You link an eligible credit or debit card, then tap to activate the restaurants where you want to earn a higher reward rate before paying with your linked card. Eligible rewards then post automatically, with no receipts to upload.

Activations last until the end of the calendar month, and you can activate up to 25 restaurants per month (plus any monthly specials). Seated's app also advertises 5% back at participating restaurants, even without an activation, provided you open the app at least once every 30 days. Higher reward rates generally require activation, so it's worth activating your favorites at the start of each month and checking the offer terms in the app.

Rewards vary by restaurant but can be up to a generous 35% back, with the rate shown on each restaurant's page before you choose to activate it. Rewards are calculated on your eligible food-and-beverage total before tax and tip, so a restaurant offering 10% back would earn you $10 in Seated rewards on a $100 meal. Since each diner earns on the share they pay with their own linked card, splitting the bill doesn't cost anyone their individual rewards.

Seated partners with more than 2,500 restaurants in certain U.S. markets. Availability varies by city and neighborhood, so check the app for participating locations and current rewards before dining, rather than relying on a fixed city list.

You can then redeem Seated rewards for gift cards in the app's store tab, with available brands to choose from including Airbnb, Amazon, Dunkin', Nordstrom, Sephora, Starbucks, Target and Uber. Because rewards can then be converted to eligible gift cards at face value, TPG values them at $1 per $1 redeemed, provided you choose a brand you'd spend with anyway and meet any minimum redemption requirement.

The catch is that Seated rewards may expire after more than 30 days without qualifying account activity, so check the app's activity and expiration rules rather than assuming opening it alone preserves your balance. Seated also says its rewards can't be combined with other restaurant promotions, third-party deals (such as those available through Groupon) or discount offers.

If you're a new member, keep an eye out for a first-meal bonus offer of up to $10 through an eligible referral link or promotional offer, though this is not guaranteed for every member.

Related: Rove adds dining and in-store rewards in major platform expansion

Resy Rewards takes a different approach than the other three programs. It does not issue a stand-alone Resy currency. Instead, eligible U.S. American Express cardmembers earn 4 additional Membership Rewards points per dollar spent at participating restaurants, on top of the points their enrolled card already earns.

To participate, you must first enroll an eligible U.S. Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points in the Rewards tab of the Resy iOS app.

You must then book a participating restaurant through the Rewards tab, complete the meal and pay with the enrolled card. Merely dining at a participating restaurant or booking it through another part of Resy will not trigger the 4 bonus points per dollar. At launch, the program is only available through the Resy iOS app, meaning Android users cannot currently use it.

The initial New York City list includes restaurants like Carne Mare, Le Crocodile, Hearth, Kiko, Opto and Le Pavillon. American Express plans to expand Resy Rewards to additional U.S. cities and select Tock venues in 2027.

On a $100 eligible restaurant purchase, Resy Rewards would provide 400 bonus Membership Rewards points. Based on our valuation of 2 cents per Membership Rewards point, that is an estimated $8 in value (or an 8% return) before accounting for the card's standard earning rate.

Related: Don't overlook Resy: How to maximize dining experiences and save money with this Amex benefit

Because OpenTable and DoorDash reward reservations with a fixed amount while Seated pays a percentage of your bill and Resy pays a fixed number of points per dollar spent, the best option depends on how much you spend. Here's a comparison for $100 in food-and-drink purchases (before tax and tip), assuming the advertised offers apply and you can use the full value of the DoorDash credits on a later order:

If you spend $200 on a meal rather than $100, the OpenTable and DoorDash rewards stay the same, while the Seated rewards as a percentage of spending will quickly increase. Resy would also double to 800 bonus points, worth an estimated $16 with TPG's valuation of Amex points.

Seated can be the most rewarding option for larger restaurant bills, especially at restaurants that offer higher reward rates. However, its value depends on the percentage offered. DoorDash's fixed credits may still provide you with a better return on smaller bills or at restaurants that offer lower Seated rewards. Resy provides a consistent 8% estimated return from its bonus points — but only at its small number of participating restaurants at launch.

Related: The dining statement credits that save me over $1,000 every year

Certain restaurant purchases can also earn credit card rewards in addition to the benefits provided by these platforms. Combining these apps with a card that earns bonus points at restaurants can be an easy way to double-dip and earn more rewards. Some of the best options currently available include:

But it gets even better. Savvy diners keen on maximizing their rewards may be able to triple-dip by booking an eligible Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables restaurant through OpenTable and paying with their Sapphire Reserve card. Doing so will allow you to earn OpenTable Regulars points plus 3 Chase Ultimate Rewards points per dollar spent on the eligible dining purchase, even if you later receive a statement credit. Qualifying purchases at participating restaurants can also trigger the separate Sapphire Reserve dining credit, worth up to $150 per half-year.

Related: How to double-, triple- or even quadruple-dip on dining rewards

Resy Rewards offers a strong, straightforward points return at participating restaurants. However, the program is launching at only a handful of New York City restaurants and is available through the Resy iOS app, so most diners will not be able to use it regularly yet.

Seated has the highest potential return for larger dining bills. A restaurant offering 15% back would earn you $30 in rewards redeemable for gift cards on a $200 dinner, while a 35% offer would earn $70. Know, though, that higher rates generally require monthly activation, and you'll need to keep your rewards account active.

DoorDash Reservations can still be the best option for smaller meals when the booking carries a strong credit. A $10 or $12 reward can beat percentage-based programs on a modest check. The catch is that rewards now vary by reservation, availability is limited to select cities and the credits are less useful if you rarely order through DoorDash.

OpenTable Regulars is the least rewarding of the four for most standard reservations, with a 100-point booking worth just 80 cents at the best U.S. redemption rate. Still, it is the most broadly available of the four in the markets where its Dining Points program operates and offers useful extras, including bonus-point tables, Gold Tables and a three-month Uber One trial for eligible Gold members. Select Chase cardholders can also receive statement credits at eligible restaurants.

There's no single best dining rewards platform for everyone, as the right choice depends on where you live, how much you spend and how often you dine out.

Resy offers a compelling points return at participating venues, but its limited launch footprint and lack of an Android app make it more of a promising option than an everyday solution right now.

Seated can deliver the biggest reward on an expensive meal, while DoorDash can be particularly rewarding on a smaller bill when the booking offers a decent credit.

As for OpenTable, it remains the most broadly available of the four in the markets where its Dining Points program operates. Its nationwide coverage, Gold perks and Chase partnership make it worth considering, especially when you travel.

Since all four cost nothing to join, you may as well sign up for them all so you are ready the next time you want to book a meal. Just remember to show up for reservations or cancel within the restaurant's deadline, as no-shows can cost you points, credits or even access.

That's some food for thought before your next night out.

#6042. Tempers flare as future of Social Security debated

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call)

If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday showed how poisonous the politics could become.

Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

“I think it’s outrageous,” said Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking important.”

Johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

"This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he said on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”

But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”

In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson said Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”

Johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

There is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson said Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

Senators on both sides of the aisle said they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

“I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability issue, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” said Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

#6041. Considering The Bilt Palladium Card? Here’s Why You Should Apply Soon…

The Bilt Palladium Card (learn more) is the most premium card in the Bilt credit card portfolio, and personally, it’s one of my all-around favorite cards (Rates & Fees). If you’ve been on the fence about picking up this very lucrative card, I’d highly recommend applying ASAP, and definitely before the end of 2026. Let me explain…

The Bilt Palladium Card is one of my favorite credit cards, and it’s the card that gets the most of my spending. Just to cover some of the very basics, the card has a $495 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers the following value proposition at the moment:

For me, the logic of picking up this card is pretty straightforward, and I’ve shared that in much more detail. The idea is that the combination of the 2x points plus 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash is an unrivaled return on spending, especially given the value of Bilt points. Spending on Bilt cards also earns you Bilt elite status, and that unlocks better Rent Day promotions.

On the most basic level, that Bilt Cash earns me 1x points per dollar spent on my housing payments (without any sort of fee), plus I take advantage of the Points Accelerator feature, which earns me an extra 1x points per dollar spent up to five times per year, by redeeming $200 in Bilt Cash. In other words, this card earns me 3x points on up to $25,000 of spending per year, plus I’m being rewarded on my housing spending.

Points with Bilt rack up really quickly, so if you spend quite a bit on credit cards, I do think this is tough to beat. And this doesn’t even account for the value of the hotel credit, as you can stack the credit card’s hotel credit with some Bilt Cash to get an even bigger discount on a hotel stay.

As I’ve covered, changes are coming to Bilt as of 2027. While the changes are being made in the name of “simplifying” things, I’d argue that it only creates even more complexity, at least for existing members. Essentially, starting in 2027, Bilt members will earn points for their housing payment as a percentage of their card spending, in lieu of earning 4% back in Bilt Cash on all their spending.

The good news is that through December 31, 2026, you can still opt into the old system for being rewarded, and that will then be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies both to existing cardmembers, and those who pick up the card before then, and select this as their earnings preference.

The idea is that if you opt into this grandfathered system and have the Bilt Palladium Card:

Just as an example, I have more Bilt Cash than I can redeem (at least as someone who is scared of helicopters, and who finds Blacklane to be overpriced even with the Bilt Cash redemption options). However, the Bilt Cash I earn gets me 1x points on all my housing payments, maxed out Points Accelerator redemptions, elevated Rent Day offers, and Lyft and Walgreens redemptions, so I get $120 in credit with each business per year.

I think the Bilt Palladium can still absolutely be worth it under the new system, where you’d be rewarded on housing payments per the below, and would also earn $600 in Bilt Cash annually (starting in 2027), but without the 4% back in the form of Bilt Cash on spending.

So if the Bilt Palladium Card has at all been on your radar, this would definitely be the time to apply. After all, this is what will allow you to maximize value on the card in the long run.

Bilt is making some program changes as of 2027, which are a mixed bag. From my perspective, the biggest loss is that cardmembers are by default being switched from a system where they earn points plus flexible Bilt Cash for their spending, to one where they earn points plus rewards at a certain rate toward housing payments.

At least for me, the old system is definitely better, and the good news is that through the end of 2026, you can continue to opt into the old system of earning points plus Bilt Cash for spending, and then that will be honored in 2027 and beyond. This applies not just to those who already have the card, but also those who open the card before the end of the year. So if the Bilt Palladium Card has been on your radar, I’d recommend applying in the near future.

#6039. Influencer Uses AI To Score American First Class Upgrade… And Overpays

There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉

Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:

What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

Go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”

ChatGPT shows you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”

Prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”

ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

You can watch the video for yourself below.

A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt)

I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:

Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:

To me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

If AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

By the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

While the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

What do you make of this AI “assistance” for a first class upgrade?

#6036. Grand Theft Auto VI and How We Spend Our Time

Your time on earth, no matter how long, is shorter than you think. Do you want to spend it doing chores in a simulated environment?

A gamer plays Grand Theft Auto VI during an unofficial launch party at OS Gaming Lounge in New York City on November 19, 2026.

Donald Trump just met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China for a tripartite global summit — and nobody has any real news to report, except for Trump, so desperate for media attention that he’s giving interviews to anyone holding a hot mic and a video camera. The lack of news is not just because of a (predictable) blackout enforced by the Chinese Communist Party, but because the collective consciousness of America has shut down for the next few days. If you thought the traditional four-day Thanksgiving Day Weekend was typically slow, get ready for a one-and-a-half-week productivity dip in the economy as the video game Grand Theft Auto VI goes live across the nation. Even National Review, as sober-minded as it is, has more than a few fans of the series on its staff.

Every periodical you might care to read — even the political or news-based ones — has brought forward its big-think “review” of the game, now available on PlayStation and Xbox. For all I know we’ll be publishing one too. But I am not a gamer — not in the modern sense of the word, although I did whip out my copy of Battletoads for the NES the other day to prove that I’ve still “got it” — and this will not be a review of GTA VI. Instead, I want to talk about time spent — and time wasted.

A gamer plays Grand Theft Auto VI during an unofficial launch party at OS Gaming Lounge in New York City on November 19, 2026.

#6035. Alaska Airlines Flight Delayed Hours After ICE Jet Bridge Brawl In Seattle

An Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”). This ended up turning into a huge jet bridge melee, leading to additional arrests, as ICE claims that someone hurled hot coffee at the officers.

In the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged. This is quite the story, as flagged by PYOK.

This incident happened on the morning of Saturday, November 21, 2026, and involves Alaska Airlines flight AS1306, scheduled to operate from Seattle (SEA) to Los Angeles (LAX).

This was first reported by a passenger on the flight, who explained that “ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding,” and went on to explain that they were “deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale.”

ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding. Now deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale @CNN @nytimes @seattletimes

Video taken from the jet bridge shows masked ICE agents trying to arrest people on the jet bridge.

Masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv

As a result of this incident, the Alaska flight ended up being delayed by hours. It was initially supposed to depart at 8:10AM and arrive at 11:01AM, but instead, departed at 11:03AM and arrived at 1:36PM.

On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

During the arrest other travelers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers—a federal crime and a felony. One passenger hurled hot coffee on the officers. Other passengers began obstructing federal officers.

The individual who threw the hot coffee was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well. She will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and a felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws. During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5

The Port of Seattle expressed its outrage about the incident, releasing the following statement:

We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson was also angry, as he held a press conference about what happened, and released the following statement:

ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities. Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics. I’ll have more to say this afternoon.

Meanwhile Alaska Airlines took a more toned down approach, and just expressed “concern,” releasing the following statement:

There’s simply no arguing that in terms of public sentiment, the tides have turned in terms of immigration enforcement, with even Trump recently admitting “I think it might be too tough.”

Q: You think your deportation policy went too far?Trump: I think it might be too tough. pic.twitter.com/NKhFjZKxnd

No matter how you feel about deportations as such, having them go down in this way for someone who simply overstayed their visa is a step too far, in my opinion. I mean, it’s one thing if we’re talking about a violent criminal on some sort of watch list, but that’s clearly not the case here.

Our four-year-old is currently at the age where he asks “why” in response to everything… and he has a lot of good questions that often make me step back and think “oh, that’s a good point.” I put myself in the situation of being on the jet bridge here as a parent, and trying to explain what was going on.

And here’s the thing — it’s one thing if these people were in uniform and identifying themselves, but when you have people who refuse to identify themselves, it’s an especially bad look. It reminds me of another incident we recently saw at Las Vegas Airport (LAS). Like, is this person being robbed in the terminal, or is this an official law enforcement operation?

A post shared by Chris Motley (@motleymodel)

On Saturday, an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by a few hours after ICE agents stormed a jet bridge to arrest someone, leading to a larger fight, which also caused more arrests. It’s one thing if such a disruptive operation were targeting a violent criminal, but is this really the way that someone who overstays a visa should be apprehended?

The Port of Seattle has expressed outrage over how this was handled, while ICE is outraged at how its “brave law enforcement” is facing increasing violence from the public.

Whatever side you are on, it is NOT ACCEPTABLE to assault any other person, especially law enforcement. You hypocrites in the comments are absolutely disgusting human beings. Are there no sane people left?

Delay flight by 3 hours, arrest several people and traumatise even more. Sounds like a proportionate response to catching one person that overstayed their visa.

I find it interesting that enforcing federal law is now verboten and releasing violent criminals is now encouraged. If you think that was a blue in November I have a million Aeroplan points valued at 2.05 cents a piece.

These THUGs need to go back to jail and not pre-tend to be police. Hopefully, the recent blue wave will be the first step in returning the United States to respect all people, since "All PEOPLE are created equal" and Project 2025 is NOT our Constitution. Your attempt at turning the US into Russia West has failed, time to retake our country! ICE OUT

Governor Ferguson went further than this article notes: he is calling for disbanding ICE entirely. I concur with that opinion. ICE has become a police agency that routinely violates more laws than it enforces. It's time that ICE, as an agency (not the agents) gets the death penalty. From a common sense perspective--whose bright idea was it to make arrests in a crowded jetway while active boarding was going on? I would hope those agents are suspended without pay while this is thoroughly investigated and eventually fired for lack of judgment, but I am not holding my breath. From a fiscally conservative point of view--ICE is a huge, money wasting bureaucracy that we don't need. They charter expensive flights to deport harmless individuals and have bought prisons and lined the pockets of private prison operators who make money by housing prisoners in horrible conditions. From a historical point of view--Let us not forget that ICE is a relatively new agency. It arose from the hysteria following 9/11, and much like the supposed WMDs in Iraq were used as an excuse to attack Iraq, ICE's creation was based on a lie. The 9/11 hijackers were all properly documented, had valid visas to be in the USA, and made a point of using their real identities. Had ICE existed prior to 9/11, it would have done nothing at all to prevent the attacks. Being against ICE is not the same thing as being against all immigration enforcement. Before ICE, we had enforcement: after ICE, we will still have enforcement but it will be appropriate. From a civil rights point of view--ICE continues to violate the rights of US citizens and legal residents on a routine basis. If they can do that to one legal resident, they can do it to ANY legal resident. If you approve of ICE now, you might want to consider what might happen if ICE still exists when a new president takes office. And, if you are on this forum, you likely travel elsewhere in the world. What goes around comes around, i.e., I would like to continue to be treated fairly outside the USA.

#6034. Citi AAdvantage Business Card Bonus: 75K Miles Welcome Offer (Double Dip Loyalty Points!)

The Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® is American’s primary co-branded business credit card. We’re currently seeing an excellent limited time welcome offer, which is in line with the highest ever offer that we’ve seen on the card.

That makes this the ideal time to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Not only that, but this is a card that many people will want, given that it’s my favorite American card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can basically double dip Loyalty Points.

Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard®

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently has a limited time welcome offer of 75,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months. This is a highest-ever offer, in line with the best bonuses I recall seeing on the card (I covered the card’s offer history below). We don’t know when this offer will be pulled.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I value AAdvantage miles at 1.5 cents each, so to me the bonus is worth $1,125. There are some incredible uses of American AAdvantage miles, including for travel on some world class partner airlines.

Just to give a few examples of AAdvantage mileage redemptions, you could redeem 57,500 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Finnair business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Helsinki (HEL)…

…or you could redeem 60,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Japan Airlines business class award from Dallas (DFW) to Tokyo (HND)…

…or you could redeem 40,000 AAdvantage miles for a one-way Etihad business class award (or 50,000 miles for an Etihad first class award) from Abu Dhabi (AUH) to Tokyo (NRT).

In each case, these tickets would typically cost many thousands of dollars, so you’re getting incredible value. When there is award availability, AAdvantage really is a program that’s tough to beat.

Also keep in mind that credit card spending will qualify for Loyalty Points (helping you earn elite status, including Gold, Platinum, Platinum Pro, or Executive Platinum), though the welcome bonus as such won’t. Upon completing minimum spending, you’d earn a minimum of 5,000 Loyalty Points. As I’ll explain below, you can even double dip the Loyalty Points you earn.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card 75,000-point offer is the best publicly available sign-up bonus that we’ve seen on the card. How do the previous Citi AAdvantage Business Card bonuses compare?

As you can see, the Citi AAdvantage Business Card publicly available welcome offer has most commonly varied from 65,000 to 75,000 miles, so you might as well apply when the offer is the best.

If you’re interested in applying for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, the typical Citi credit card application restrictions apply, including that you can be approved for at most one Citi card every eight days, and at most two Citi cards every 65 days.

On top of that, the bonus isn’t available to those who have received a new account bonus on this exact card in the past 48 months. Eligibility is unrelated to having any other American Airlines credit cards.

There’s not a published credit score you need to get approved for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Ideally I’d hope to have a credit score of 700+, but people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been denied.

If you’re concerned about Chase’s 5/24 rule, note that applying for a Citi business card generally won’t count toward that limit. I should also mention that at least anecdotally, this card seems to be quite easy to get approved for.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card has an annual fee that’s waived for the first year, so you can “try” the card before you have to pay a fee. While the fee after that is technically still $99, it’s increasing to $150 as of January 24, 2027, so that’s what you’d pay on account renewal. There’s no cost to add employee cards for authorized users.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card offers a variety of valuable perks, including:

Above I mentioned how the Citi AAdvantage Business Card is the best card for earning AAdvantage elite status. The reason is because through December 31, 2028, the card essentially lets you double dip Loyalty Points. If you add an authorized user, their spending will earn 1x Loyalty Points per dollar spent for both their own account, and for the primary cardmember’s account. So this is a way to essentially get two-for-one elite status qualification, which is awesome.

With the annual fee increasing as of January 2027, the card will also pick up several valuable new perks, including the following:

Read a detailed review of the Citi AAdvantage Business Card.

The Citi AAdvantage Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus of 75,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months. This is a great offer on a valuable card that even has its annual fee waived for the first year.

This is also my favorite card for earning AAdvantage elite status, since you can essentially earn Loyalty Points for two members at once. Authorized user spending earns Loyalty Points for the authorized user’s AAdvantage account, and also for the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage account.

Anyone plan to pick up the Citi AAdvantage Business Card with 75K miles?

As much as I love the holiday season, it's my least favorite time to travel. Flights and accommodations are expensive, airports are at their busiest and winter storms can upend even the best-laid plans.

A credit card can't help your family pack lighter or ensure your flight departs on time. But the right benefits can lessen the sting from some of travel's most predictable pain points.

Here are the cards that can make the biggest difference during a hectic holiday trip, organized by the problem they solve.

Few travel fees are more annoying than paying extra to bring your socks with you — especially now that roundtrip bag fees can feel higher than the cost of the clothes inside.

For a family checking multiple bags, this may be the most immediately valuable benefit on this list. A card with a relatively modest annual fee can pay for itself during holiday travel alone.

Many airline credit cards offer a free checked bag, so start with the airline you fly most.

Higher-fee airline cards often match or exceed the checked-bag benefits shown here.

Many of the same airline cards that waive bag fees also provide priority boarding benefits. On a packed holiday flight, I'll gladly get in line early if it keeps my carry-on out of the gate-check pile.

The $895 annual fee (see rates and fees) offers another way to lower the cost of bags or boarding. Its up to $200 annual airline incidental credit can reimburse eligible expenses such as checked bag and seat selection fees with one selected qualifying airline (enrollment required). This is a useful way for existing cardmembers to absorb a holiday expense.

The (see rates and fees) offers a broader alternative: Its $300 annual travel credit applies automatically to eligible travel purchases, including checked bag fees.

Related: Which airline credit cards offer the best priority boarding perks?

Ever spend more time in airport security than you do on the flight itself? TSA PreCheck, Global Entry and Clear+ earn their keep throughout November and December.

PreCheck provides expedited screening at eligible U.S. airports; Global Entry includes PreCheck and adds expedited processing when returning to the U.S. from abroad; and Clear+ uses biometric identity verification to speed up the document-check step of security (so some travelers use it alongside PreCheck).

And for travelers who frequently cross between the U.S. and Canada, Nexus can speed up passport control.

You don't necessarily need a premium card to get these application fees reimbursed. Options include:

I like this benefit because it works regardless of which airline you're flying and gives you something that's often in limited supply: time. Just apply well before your trip because Trusted Traveler applications take some time to process. You can't open a card on Monday and expect to breeze through security on Friday.

The information for the U.S. Bank Altitude Connect has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

A lounge won't make a delayed flight leave sooner, but a power outlet, snacks and a drink make the wait easier.

These lounge cards offer different benefits:

* Up to 10 visits per eligible Platinum Card, per year to the Delta Sky Club or to Grab and Go when traveling on a same-day Delta-operated flight

I've had all of these over the years, although lately my favorite card for lounge access is the Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite. The card's Priority Pass membership still provides credits at participating airport restaurants, which can be helpful when traditional lounges are full or there's nowhere left to sit.

There's a broader lesson there, too: don't choose a card based solely on how many lounges its network advertises. Check whether your airports have participating locations, whether there are restrictions on when you can visit and if it costs extra to bring your travel companions.

The information for the Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

Related: Is the Amex Platinum worth the annual fee?

Some premium-card credits seem easy to overlook until you arrive at midnight with no energy to navigate public transportation and ride-hailing fares are surging.

Food-delivery credits are also surprisingly useful at the hotel. I recently had Uber Eats delivered to my hotel because taking a cranky kid to dinner wasn't my idea of a good time.

For Uber users, both the and stand out. The Gold offers up to $120 in Uber Cash annually (distributed as up to $10 each month), while the Platinum offers up to $200 in Uber Cash annually (up to $15 each month, plus an additional $20 in December) for U.S. Uber rides and Uber Eats orders.

Uber Cash will only be deposited into one Uber account when you add the Amex Gold or Amex Platinum as a payment method and redeem with any Amex card.

Platinum cardmembers can also receive up to a $120 statement credit for an auto-renewing Uber One membership, Uber's paid membership program for ride and delivery savings (enrollment required).

The counters with up to $420 in DoorDash credits (a monthly $15 promo for any eligible order plus two $10 nonrestaurant promos, through Dec. 31, 2029).

Its complimentary DashPass membership (activate by Dec. 31, 2029) also unlocks Lyft Go at no additional cost, allowing you to earn Lyft credits on eligible rides. Separately, Sapphire Reserve cardholders receive up to $10 in monthly Lyft ride credits through Sep. 30, 2027. (You'll need to link your DoorDash and Lyft accounts and claim Lyft Go.)

These credits alone are not reasons to pay hundreds of dollars in annual fees. But they can be genuinely useful when you're otherwise staring down an expensive ride or going to bed hungry.

Hotel timing benefits are especially useful when checkout is at 11 a.m., your flight leaves after dinner and no one wants to tote an overstuffed diaper bag around for six hours while your toddler desperately needs a nap.

There are two ways a credit card can help: through a premium hotel-booking program or automatic hotel elite status.

Those looking for boutique hotel experiences can access The Edit by Chase Travel℠ with their . These bookings provide benefits like daily breakfast for two people and a $100 property credit. When available, early check-in, late checkout and room upgrades are also offered. Cardholders receive up to $500 annually in statement credits for eligible prepaid The Edit bookings (of at least two nights; split into two credits of up to $250 each).

Similarly, cardmembers can receive up to $300 in statement credits biannually (up to $600 per calendar year) on eligible prepaid bookings through Fine Hotels + Resorts, The Hotel Collection and Airbnb Luxe through American Express Travel®.

FHR bookings include guaranteed 4 p.m. checkout, daily breakfast for two and property or experience credits. Room upgrades and early check-in are also offered (subject to availability).

(THC and Airbnb Luxe bookings require a minimum stay of two consecutive nights. Beginning Jan. 1, 2027, FHR bookings will also require at least two nights to qualify for the lodging statement credit.)

These programs can be valuable when a nicer property is already part of the plan or you have annual hotel credits to use. Just don't let a possible upgrade or a few extra hours rationalize a room that costs twice as much as the hotel across the street.

Many hotel credit cards offer complimentary elite status. For example, the $95-per-year (see rates and fees) includes Discoverist status, which comes with 2 p.m. late checkout (when available).

Top-tier Globalist status extends that to a 4 p.m. checkout. The Hyatt card can help you work toward it with five qualifying-night credits each year plus two additional credits for every $5,000 spent.

Related: World of Hyatt Credit Card review: My favorite mid-tier hotel card

Hotel breakfast is one of those expenses that seems harmless until you're buying it for several people for several mornings.

These cards can help lower breakfast costs:

cardmembers can enroll in Hilton Gold status and receive breakfast or food-and-beverage benefits rather than having to apply for a Hilton card separately.

Rental car status is rarely about an upgrade from a sedan to an SUV, especially during a sold-out holiday week. The most valuable benefit is simply getting into a car and leaving the airport while everyone else is still waiting at the counter.

Capital One Venture X cardholders can enroll in Hertz President's Circle status**, which offers benefits including skip-the-line privileges, a wider vehicle selection, potential upgrades and a free additional driver. Meanwhile, the $95 Venture Rewards offers lower-tier Hertz Five Star** status.

cardholders receive Avis Preferred Plus and National Executive status, and cardmembers can enroll in complimentary elite status with Avis, Hertz and National.

In every case, the key is to enroll. Sign up and confirm your status appears in your account before you leave home.

**Upon enrollment, accessible through the Capital One website or mobile app, eligible cardholders will remain at that status level through the duration of the offer. Please note, enrolling through the normal Hertz Gold Plus Rewards enrollment process (i.e., at hertz.com) will not automatically detect a cardholder as being eligible for the program, and cardholders will not be automatically upgraded to the applicable status tier. Additional terms apply.

Related: How to stack Venture X earning and Hertz elite benefits

These perks are only useful if they are ready when you need them. Before your trip:

Related: 4 things you really need to do now in advance of holiday travel

For holiday travel, the best card isn't necessarily the one with the longest list of premium benefits; it's the one that solves the problem most likely to cost you money or patience. A family checking several bags may save more with a $95 airline card than an $895 premium card, while someone planning a dream trip may want every perk they can get.

Opening an expensive card solely to make one trip less miserable isn't the play here. But if you are already paying a premium annual fee, this is the time to use the benefits you've paid for all year.

Related: 10 real-world tips you need for flying this holiday season

#6032. Free AAdvantage Business Program 10K Bonus Miles New Member Promotion

AAdvantage Business is American’s free small business rewards program, and if you’re eligible and fly American with any frequency, it’s absolutely worth participating (it essentially lets you earn one bonus Loyalty Point and AAdvantage mile per eligible dollar spent on flights, beyond what you usually earn).

At the moment, we’re seeing a new member bonus for those who register for an account, making it the ideal time to sign-up, if you haven’t done so already. In particular, this pairs very nicely with the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (learn more) limited time welcome bonus, which offers 75,000 AAdvantage miles upon completing minimum spending.

Through December 31, 2026, the AAdvantage Business program is offering 10,000 AAdvantage bonus miles to anyone who registers for the program with promotion code BNS10K. Bonus miles will post within six to eight weeks following the successful enrollment in the program.

For what it’s worth, we did see a bonus of 15,000 miles several weeks ago, but that’s no longer available, and this bonus is much better than usual, as there isn’t ordinarily a standard bonus for becoming a member.

I should mention that in order to be eligible to participate in the AAdvantage Business program, you need to have a business in the United States or Canada with a Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) or Business Number. However, even small businesses are eligible for this program, so that’s pretty awesome.

There’s no activity required to earn the 10,000 bonus miles in your AAdvantage Business account. Let me emphasize that with AAdvantage Business, miles are accrued to the business, and can then be shared with any company member, so they can redeem through their personal AAdvantage account.

There’s one main catch with the AAdvantage Business program, which is that in order to actually redeem the rewards you earn, you need to meet one of two activity requirements:

There’s the opportunity to really maximize value here by taking advantage of two promotions. The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently has a huge limited time welcome offer of 75,000 AAdvantage miles after spending $5,000 within the first five months, and the annual fee is even waived for the first 12 months.

So there’s value to taking advantage of both of these promotions:

There are many reasons to apply for the Citi AAdvantage Business Card, and the unique double dipping opportunity cardmembers are eligible for, which has made this one of my go-to cards for everyday spending.

The AAdvantage Business program is offering 10,000 bonus miles to new businesses that sign-up with promotion code BNS10K. Assuming you’re eligible, this is absolutely worth taking advantage of.

The only catch is that in order to actually cash out those miles from your business account, you need to have qualifying activity. That could include having five travelers spend $5,000 in a year, or there’s the easier option, which is just to pick up the Citi AAdvantage Business Card. Just make sure you open the business account before you apply for the credit card, so that your card will then automatically correctly link to the account.

Do you plan on taking advantage of this AAdvantage Business promotion?

#6029. Trump banks on personal relationships moving Putin, Xi toward U.S. interests

Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images)

That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

“It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

Trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he launched a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

His interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

Both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

“I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump said as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

“You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”

Trump, who was convicted by a New York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

“In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

Other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of issues, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

“This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”

Nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He said it was “important” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”

“The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”

Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers said they doubted very much would come from it.

“I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

“I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”

Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

“Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal said Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”

On spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to quickly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

“You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”

John M. Donnelly and Jackie Wang contributed to this report.
